properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 5:31PM MDT until September 15 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 531 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated between 0.50 and 1.00 inches
of rain has fallen across portions of the San Rafael Swell, including
Muddy Creek, Ramp, Cistern, Ding, Dang, Bell, Little Wildhorse, Crack
and Chute Canyons. Flash flooding is ongoing across within these
drainages.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of slot canyons and normally
dry washes.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
The Chute of Muddy Creek, Little Wildhorse Canyon, Ding and Dang
Canyons, Crack and Chute Canyons, as well as portions of Goblin
Valley State Park.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

expected.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Omaha/Valley has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Iowa...

East Nishnabotna River At Red Oak affecting Montgomery County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...East Nishnabotna River at Red Oak.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Lowland flooding begins along the west
bank.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:00 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 19.7 feet just after midnight
tonight. It will then fall below flood stage by late tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.6
feet on 06/15/1980.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 4:42PM MDT until September 15 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 442 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
moderate rain over the western portion of the Frijoles Burn Scar as
well as areas west of the burn scar to including Cundiyo. Between
0.50 and 0.75 inches of rain have fallen over the western portions of
the burn scar, with up to 1.5 inches along Highway 503 southwest of
Cundiyo. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.50 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact the Rio Frijoles,
Rio Medio and Chimayo Creek as well as Camino del Canon, County Road
127 and Camino del Molino. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials. Flooding will also impact
Cundiyo and Highway 503.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Frijoles Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Frijoles Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chimayo, Cundiyo, Rio Chiquito, Nambe Pueblo, Nambe Lake and
Cordova.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the Frijoles Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.
